reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the three refunds Alpha reported (orders 260, 263, 265). Starting by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly: orders 260, 263, and 265 with the same amounts. Next I need the list of orders to find which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The customers in the orders are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 29089 cents. Its orders total 25692 + 20673 = 46365, and refunds on 260 and 263 total 8294 + 8982 = 17276, giving 29089, which matches. I'll continue with birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance is 62075 cents. Its orders total 32750 + 29325 = 62075 with no refunds, which matches. Next I need cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 39438 matches its orders (33488 + 16853 = 50341) minus the refund on order 265 (10903). All three customers reconcile, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme for 29089 cents.
Acme's payout of 29089 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 62075 matches its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt is the only remaining customer. Its net balance of 39438 matches orders 262 and 265 (33488 + 16853 = 50341) minus the refund on 265 (10903), so I'll record its payout.
All three customers' payouts were recorded successfully, and each matched its reconciled net balance. The batch is complete.
